title: perf(canary): add continuous regression detector and rollout-guard CI job
author: Maya Thompson
description:
Motivation: We need automated, repeatable canaries that detect latency/throughput regressions before full rollouts and block unsafe deployments. This PR adds a continuous regression-detector pipeline and a rollout-guard CI job that integrates with our protected-branch rules.

What this does: Adds a perf-canary runner, a CI job (ci/perf-canary.yml), infra hooks for the rollout-guard, and a small dashboard + docs. The canary runs a short synthetic workload against candidate builds, compares summary statistics (p50/p95/throughput) to a rolling baseline, and fails the check if a statistically significant regression or >X% cost-latency tradeoff is detected. The check can block merges (protected branch) or trigger automatic rollback during automated deploys.

Design highlights: Uses a lightweight, reproducible harness (tools/perf-canary/runner.py) that: generates representative request traces (sampling distributions derived from production traces), warms caches (KV prefix warmup), and runs multiple iterations to estimate p50/p95 and throughput. Baselines are pulled from our TSDB (Prometheus) using a 7-day rolling window and a median+MAD-based baseline with configurable sensitivity. Statistical test is bootstrapped percentile comparison with configurable alpha; thresholds and sample sizes are configurable via ci/perf-canary.yml and infra/rollouts/guard.tf.

Rollout guard behavior: When the canary job runs as part of a release pipeline it emits a GitHub check with structured metadata (baseline-id, metrics, delta-percent, p-value). If the job fails, the rollout-guard marks the deployment as blocked and creates a Linear ticket (automated) with the top failing metrics and traces. For PR-triggered runs the job posts a summary comment and a compact artifact with trace snippets.

Testing & rollout: Local dev: python -m tools.perf_canary.runner --local-mock to run against a mock model serving fixture. Staging: the pipeline will run against the staging fleet for 24 hours to collect baselines; then will be enabled as a required check on release branches. Rollout plan: opt-in for 2 weeks for canary-as-check, then flip to required on main for release tags.

Checklist:
- [x] perf-canary runner and CI job
- [x] rollout-guard terraform hook and RBAC for CI user
- [x] dashboard panels and alert rules (dashboards/perf-canary.json)
- [x] docs (docs/perf/canary.md)
- [x] unit + e2e harness tests

Backwards compatibility: This is opt-in initially and controlled by protected-branch checks and Terraform. No runtime changes to serving code unless the canary harness is explicitly enabled.

Related: Linear ENG-1987 (canary infra), SRE-34 (incidents -> perf alerts).
commits_summary: a1f3b7d: add perf-canary CI workflow and entrypoint
b92d71c: implement runner harness with warmup + sampling logic
c7e4a11: add baseline fetcher and bootstrap comparator
d44f2a9: rollout-guard TF hook + GitHub check integration
e5b8c3f: dashboards and docs + unit tests
release_notes: Adds an automated continuous performance canary and a rollout-guard CI check that can block deployments on statistically significant latency/throughput regressions. Configurable sensitivity and opt-in before enforcing on main.
review_comments: Ravi Patel (requested changes): The harness looks solid but we need to ensure cache-warmup mimics production KV prefix usage; please add a mode that replays cached prefixes from a sampled trace.
Maya Thompson (author): Added --replay-prefixes flag and a small sampled-prefix generator to runner.py; updated tests to cover warmup path.
Elena García: Please make thresholds configurable per-channel (hosted/dedicated/private) — latency sensitivity differs across fleets.
Maya Thompson: Thresholds pulled from infra/rollouts/guard.tf now, default per-channel overrides added.
Chris Wong (approved): CI passes locally and on staging; good to merge once infra RBAC review is green.
Infra-Security Bot: Detected new IAM binding for ci-rollout-service-account; manual review completed and approved by security.
CI: initial run had a flaky test (tests/perf/test_runner_integration.py) failing under concurrent load; rerun fixed the flake after adding a short jitter between test instances.
Maya Thompson: Addressed flake, increased default sample retries and added jitter. Re-ran CI and all checks green.
notes: Edge cases: small models with <20ms p50 are more sensitive to noise; runner uses higher iteration counts for those models by default.
To opt-out: remove perf-canary required check from the branch protection rules or set canary.enabled=false in release pipeline config.
Follow-ups: add automated story extraction to Linear when multiple metrics fail to help prioritize regressions (ENG-2003).
